title: Unconditional class-number tables beyond Watkins (h > 100) from 003's 7/8 half-plane + Tatuzawa
summary: 003's Lean-formalized Dirichlet zero-free half-plane Re s > 7/8 meets the zero-free hypothesis of Tatuzawa's explicit Siegel bound (EKN Lemma 3) for every D, giving h(D) > 0.0767 sqrt|D|/log|D| for all fundamental |D| > e^11.2 with no exception. That makes complete lists of imaginary quadratic fields of class number h computable unconditionally: |D| <= 7.1e8 for h <= 100, 2e10 for h <= 457, 2^40 for h <= 2900. Brute force from this bound alone reproduced Watkins's table for h <= 10 exactly.

targets.name: Sage cm.py largest_fundamental_disc_with_class_number (h<=100 only, 'unconditional results much harder')

beneficiaries: SageMath/LMFDB CM and class-number functionality (cm_orders, cm_j_invariants for degree >100), CM/Heegner-point researchers, anyone citing Watkins h<=100 as the unconditional frontier
first_step: Write a 2-page note with the bound, the constants (0.655, e^11.2) and the h<=10 replication. Get an expert (e.g. Watkins/Klaise/Jacobson) to confirm Tatuzawa's constants via Hoffstein's 'On the Siegel-Tatuzawa theorem'. Then open a Sage PR adding an optional unconditional bound B(h) that replaces the h<=100 NotImplementedError.
measurement: Rows of the unconditional (h, #D, max|D|) table beyond h=100 produced and cross-checked against the GRH tables of Holmin et al. Sage doctests pass. Largest h certified (target h<=457 from qfbclassno-certified range, h<=2900 by reusing the 2^40 tabulation).
risks: Tatuzawa's 1951 constants need an independent check (Hoffstein revisited the theorem). The B(h) bound is about 50x the GRH bound, so the computation is cluster-scale (about 5e9 discriminants to 2e10). Modest user base. 003 itself is low-risk (Lean, Mathlib-only statement).

title: Prepare LMFDB/Sage for the full BSD formula in rank <= 1 (002): pending-review flag, no assertion yet
summary: If 002 holds, Sha_an = #Sha for all 3.29M LMFDB rank-<=1 curves (86.1%), and Sage prove_BSD() could return [] for every certified rank-<=1 curve. Today prove_BSD already certifies about 89-91% of rank-<=1 isogeny classes at small conductor; the residual is almost all p = 3, and Sha_an = 1 for 99 of 100 open cases. The claim is extraordinary and unformalized (about 340 pages across 3 manuscripts plus the 130-page 006 dependency), so the right action is expert review plus a display-only note, not a flag change.

targets.name: Sage BSD.py prove_BSD (returns primes where BSD(E,p) unproven)
Sage sha_tate.py Sha.an ('BSD conjectural order of Sha')
LMFDB web_ec.py BSD formula '=' for r_an<2
LMFDB ec-curve.html BSD invariants / analytic Sha / BSD formula

beneficiaries: LMFDB users, arithmetic-statistics researchers who condition on BSD, Cremona ecdata, Sage/Magma/PARI documentation
first_step: Open an LMFDB discussion issue asking the editorial board to commission review of [B], [C], exact-bsd and 006. Propose a display-only knowl sentence ('claimed in an unrefereed 2026 preprint'). Do not change sha_is_exact or prove_BSD output until refereed.
measurement: Number of independent expert reports. After acceptance: share of rank-<=1 LMFDB pages with a proven Sha tag, which requires exact L'(E,1) for rank 1 beyond N=5000.
risks: Extraordinary claim; about 470 interlocking unformalized pages with mutual citations among companions; nonstandard ultralimit constructions; BSD is one of the clusters with Oct-7 repairs; no Mathlib Selmer/Sha infrastructure, so no Lean check for years. Premature adoption would contaminate a reference database.

title: Fix two crash bugs in Sage prove_BSD (secs_dc keyword; tuple item assignment)
summary: While measuring the 002 gap, I found that prove_BSD crashes on rank-0 curves that reach its 'try harder' branch. It calls heegner_index_bound(..., secs_dc=...), which has no such parameter (15 of 659 classes at N 1000-1200, e.g. 1014e1, plus 6600e1). Separately, the Kato block assigns into a tuple (BSD.bounds[p][1] = ...; curve 1058d1). These are independent of the preprints and fixable now.

targets.name: BSD.py L805 tuple item assignment (also pattern at L660)

beneficiaries: Sage users running prove_BSD; any future 002 certification sweep
first_step: Open a Sage issue and PR. Drop or plumb secs_dc (heegner_index_bound has no time limit argument). Replace BSD.bounds[p][1] = (low, ...) with BSD.bounds[p] = (low, min(BSD.bounds[p][1], bd)), likewise at L660. Add 1014e1 and 1058d1 as doctests.
measurement: prove_BSD completes on 1014e1, 1050c1, 1058d1, 6600e1. Crash count in a 1000-1200 sweep goes from 16 to 0.
risks: Minimal. The secs_dc branch may then run long, and may need a real time limit.

title: LMFDB imaginary-quadratic completeness: unconditional for 14 fields now (Caraiani-Newton); remaining 18 only with 030
summary: LMFDB says its imaginary-quadratic elliptic-curve tables are complete only 'assuming modularity'. Caraiani-Newton already prove modularity over K when X_0(15)(K) is finite. I certified that this holds for 14 of the 32 LMFDB complete-range fields (d = -3,-4,-8,-15,-19,-20,-23,-31,-35,-47,-79,-83,-87,-91), so the caveat can be lifted there today. The other 18 (including 2.0.7.1, -11, -43, -67, -163) would need 030, a single unformalized 30-page paper.

targets.name: LMFDB knowl rcs.cande.ec ('Assuming modularity, the database is complete')

beneficiaries: LMFDB editors and users of the 455k imaginary-quadratic curves; Bianchi modular forms community
first_step: File an LMFDB issue proposing per-field completeness wording: unconditional for the 14 CN-covered fields (no preprint needed), 'claimed in an unrefereed preprint' for the other 18.
measurement: Knowl updated. Number of fields with an unconditional completeness statement (0 now, 14 immediately, 32 after 030 is refereed).
risks: 030 is unformalized, uses CN's lifting theorem plus a new geometric prime switch, and has had no expert review. LMFDB completeness also depends on correct Bianchi-form computations. The 14-field part is independent of OpenAI.

title: Docs note: deterministic square roots / Miller test unconditional (003), with the numbers that show it is galactic
summary: 003 makes n(p) <= C(log p)^A unconditional (A=32 per the paper; C uncomputed), so Tonelli-Shanks with a scanned non-residue and Miller's test become provably deterministic polynomial time. Numerically useless: even with C=1, at 2048 bits the bound is 10^18.6-10^94.3 times Bach's GRH bound. It beats explicit Burgess-type bounds only above 200-1205 bits. FLINT's 2^20 non-residue cap is justified up to about 1045 bits on GRH, but unconditionally only to 59 bits (Trevino) or about 20 bits (003). Textbook and documentation statements change; code does not.

targets.name: FLINT flint_mpn_sqrtmod doc ('negligible probability' for n(p) > 2^20)
FLINT sqrtmod.c non-residue scan with 2^20 cap

beneficiaries: Textbook authors (Galbraith, Crandall-Pomerance, Cohen, Shoup), Wikipedia, complexity theorists
first_step: Short note or Wikipedia edits stating unconditional deterministic polynomial time (via 003 + BIMS) alongside the crossover table; no library PRs.
measurement: Textbook errata and Wikipedia statements updated with the caveat that constants are uncomputed and the bound is galactic.
risks: Overclaiming practical relevance; C is never computed.

title: Coding-theory results stated 'under Artin's conjecture': sort into infinitude-only (now unconditional via 029) vs density
summary: 2024-25 asymptotic double-circulant, four-circulant, LCD and hull code results (e.g. arXiv:2401.07017) still assume Artin's conjecture to obtain infinitely many prime lengths m with q primitive mod m. 029 supplies infinitely many such m for each admissible base, enough for asymptotic existence. Results that need positive density stay conditional. BIKE/HQC parameters never needed the conjecture.

targets.name: Double/four circulant codes under Artin's conjecture

beneficiaries: Coding theorists working on quasi-cyclic / double-circulant asymptotics
first_step: Compile 10-20 theorems stated under Artin's conjecture and classify which only need infinitely many primes.
measurement: Number of theorems that become unconditional.
risks: 029 is unformalized (92 pp.) with an extraordinary uniform Hecke strip; only prime moduli and x/log^2 x density.

title: DO NOT PURSUE: '003 removes GRH from class-group computations' (PARI bnfinit/quadclassunit, Magma ClassGroup, Sage proof=False, FLINT qfb_exponent_grh, CSI-FiSh)
summary: Bach-type generator bounds for Cl(K) need GRH for the Hecke L-functions of non-genus class-group characters of K. 003 covers only Dirichlet L-functions and Hecke L-functions of Q(sqrt-3). A fixed zero-free half-plane would anyway give only a (log|d|)^O(1) bound with uncomputed constants, not 6 log^2|d|. All GRH flags stay.

targets.name: Sage number_field.py pari_bnf proof flag ('if False, assume GRH')

beneficiaries: CAS maintainers and isogeny-crypto engineers (avoids a false certification)
first_step: None; state the negative in any 003 announcement.
risks: Misreading 003 as 'GRH proved' could lead someone to drop bnfcertify.

title: DO NOT PURSUE: '029's cyclotomic Hecke strip transfers to class-group characters of quadratic fields' (triage error)
summary: Artin factorization only re-expresses zeta of an abelian extension of F through Hecke characters of F. 029 covers Hecke characters of cyclotomic F, hence (Kronecker-Weber) L-functions of abelian extensions of Q and of abelian extensions of cyclotomic fields, which is how 142 uses it. The Hilbert/ring class field of an imaginary quadratic K is generalized dihedral over Q, non-abelian once Cl(K) has exponent > 2, so non-genus class-group characters are not covered; only genus characters are. Even if they were, (log|d|)^{10^6} beats Minkowski only above 5e7-bit discriminants and Hafner-McCurley only above 4.5e13 bits.

targets.name: 029 Theorem thm:hecke-zero-free (cyclotomic F containing mu_12 only)
142 legitimate use: Kummer extension of Q(mu_12q)

beneficiaries: Anyone tempted to claim unconditional Bach bounds for quadratic class groups
first_step: Correct the b04 triage record for 029.

title: DO NOT PURSUE: implement deterministic factoring (142) or deterministic sqrt via 003 in FLINT/PARI/OpenSSL
summary: 142's O(((n+1)log p)^{10^12}) bound and 003's (log p)^{8..32} non-residue bound (C uncomputed) are galactic. Mean n(p) is 3-4 for random 256-2048-bit primes (max 23 over 560 primes). Randomized Cantor-Zassenhaus and the existing scans are what everyone uses and will keep using.

title: 004: one-line OSCAR doc note (Q-realizability undecidable); tensor rank over Q undecidable via Schaefer-Stefankovic
summary: OSCAR's is_realizable only claims decisions over some field of characteristic 0 (minimal primes) or GF(p)/GF(q). realization_space(ground_ring=QQ) returns an ideal and makes no claim about Q-points, so nothing becomes false. 004 plus Sturmfels makes Q-realizability undecidable; a sentence mirroring OSCAR's existing 'undecidable in general' notes would help users. Schaefer-Stefankovic's poly-time reduction from ETR(F) to tensor rank over F (all fields) makes tensor rank over Q undecidable given 004.

targets.name: Schaefer-Stefankovic, The Complexity of Tensor Rank

beneficiaries: Matroid and tensor-rank researchers; OSCAR users
first_step: After expert review of 004, submit a one-sentence OSCAR doc PR and a note to the tensor-rank community.
risks: 004 is unformalized and depends on the 2-converse (006 chain) and 2-adic Fontaine-Mazur (010). No software actually claimed a decision procedure over Q.

title: DO NOT PURSUE: 011/012/021 smoothness laws and Jacobsthal bound in prime generation / twin-smooth searches
summary: Asymptotic distribution laws with no rate (011, 012) and an existence bound with ineffective C (021) certify nothing at 2^256-4096-bit sizes. OpenSSL/GMP prime generation and SQIsign/B-SIDH twin-smooth searches are unchanged.
